rules.IN: New readings arrive with consent; the Orchestrator gives them to Guardian
rules.G0: No rule met → no alarm; Navigator checks what screening is due
rules.G1: Resting heart rate 120+ for 10+ minutes while inactive (device high-heart-rate alert) → Noa prompts a speech and symptom check by itself; doctor review today
rules.L1: Glucose under 3.0 mmol/L (level 2 hypoglycaemia, ADA) → treat with fast sugar, recheck in 15 minutes; medicine review within 24 hours
rules.L2: Glucose 3.0–3.8 mmol/L (level 1, ADA) → review at the next diabetes visit
rules.U1: Every pathway item carries an urgency level and a due-by date; urgent items are escalated even if the person says “not now”
rules.G2: Irregular-rhythm alerts → heart rhythm test (ECG) first in the offer; if irregular for 10+ min tonight → Voice checks now
rules.G3: Resting heart rate under 40 → Voice checks now
rules.B1: Blood pressure 180/120 or more → same-day doctor review
rules.B2: Blood pressure 140/90 or more → blood pressure plan at screening
rules.W1: BMI 30 or more → weight support in the plan
rules.A1: Under 4,000 steps a day → activity plan
rules.V1: Speech clearly changed or face or arm weakness (BE-FAST stroke signs) → see a doctor immediately at the emergency department; screening paused
rules.V2: Chest pain or fainting with a racing heart → see a doctor immediately at the emergency department; screening paused
rules.V3: Speech a little different → repeat once; still different → nurse video call within 1 hour
rules.V4: Speech as usual and no red flags → not an emergency; rhythm test within 48 hours
rules.N1: Offer only programmes the person is eligible for; the one the signals call for first
rules.N2: A barrier is found → match the support (time, place, language, why), not another reminder
rules.N3: “Not now” → no reminders for 3 months; it stays in the passport
rules.F1: Heart risk 20%+ (Framingham, ages 30–74, no heart attack or stroke) → doctor review within 2 weeks
rules.R1: A result outside the range → the right team within 2 weeks
rules.H1: Every diagnosis and treatment is decided by a clinician
rules.C1: Relatives see only what the person chooses to share
rules.X1: One person’s result can move up a relative’s screening, without sharing details
rules.D1: Every flag shows its main factors, its data source and how certain it is. A flag is a population priority, not a diagnosis
rules.P1: Only authorised data is used; the person can switch optional data, such as genomic results, off at any time
rules.Q1: Speech check: as usual → continue; a little different → repeat once; clearly changed → stop and advise seeing a doctor immediately
rules.S1: Population view: groups under 10 are hidden, and rates without enough data are not shown
rules.H2: Symptoms are not screening: a new symptom goes to a doctor’s appointment, not a screening queue
rules.T1: The pathway follows the guideline for age and sex; family history or genetic risk adds a referral that the doctor decides on
rules.T2: The pathway is fitted to the person’s time, place, language and clinician preference, without changing what is offered
rules.K2: Child development and growth outside the age range → assessment offered (demo thresholds)

detect.name: Detect
detect.title: 1 · Detect
detect.body: Noa Guardian watches {{name}}’s devices against {{name}}’s own normal and reads the last personal record and the family health record. An unusual pattern sends {{name}} a prompt; every flag shows its reasons, source and certainty (rule D1). Noa then waits: nothing moves on until the person starts it.
detect.you: Read the alert, then start the check when you are ready.

protect.name: Protect
protect.title: 2 · Protect
protect.body: Before acting, Noa confirms which data it may use and who may see the pathway. Optional data, such as a genomic result, can be switched off, and Noa drops it from the flags (rule P1).
protect.you: Choose the data and who may see the pathway.

home.name: Home screening
home.title: 3 · Home screening
home.body: A two-minute self-service check at home. Adults: the Noa Speech Check against their own voice, then questions the record cannot answer (symptoms, how and when). Children: short questions for the parent, for the child’s age.
home.you: Speak or use a sample, then answer as the person.

pathway.name: Right pathway
pathway.title: 4 · Right pathway
pathway.body: Noa Navigator builds the pathway from the guideline for age and sex, then fits it to {{name}}’s life: time, place, language, clinician. Population priority (what Noa may book) is shown apart from clinical decisions (what only the doctor decides).
pathway.you: Book it, change the time, ask why, or say not now.

referral.name: Referral
referral.title: 5 · Referral
referral.body: Bookings are made, the referral reaches the clinic before the visit, and the recall date is set. The Government agent counts the case without names (reach, recommendation, uptake by segment).
referral.you: Read the referral. Then try another person or a test case below.

chat.emergency: If anyone has slurred speech, face or arm weakness, chest pain or confusion, they should see a doctor immediately at the emergency department.
chat.emergencyActive: {{name}} has been advised to see a doctor now at the emergency department. Please help {{name}} get there, or call 998 if that is not safe. Screening is paused until a doctor has seen {{name}}.
chat.working: I’m working on {{name}}’s screening now ({{stage}}). I’ll message the family here when something is booked or needs action.
chat.idle: Tap anyone in the family tree and I’ll check what is due for them. New messages for the family appear here.

s0.title: Saeed · racing heart, auto-prompted check (start here)
s0.context: 64, type 2 diabetes. His watch reads 128 bpm at rest for 22 minutes (usual 66–76). Nobody presses anything: Noa spots the pattern and prompts the check.
s0.try: Next › all the way. The first speech try is slightly slurred (Amber); the repeat is his usual voice.
s0.expect: Auto-prompt (G1) → speech Amber, then Green → no red flags → doctor review today first; then eye and kidney checks bundled at his diabetes clinic, bowel kit and flu vaccine, each with an urgency and due date.

s2.title: Saeed · speech clearly changed
s2.context: Same racing heart, but the speech check is clearly slurred.
s2.expect: Red (V1), urgency immediate: Noa pauses screening and advises seeing a doctor now at the emergency department. Noa calls nobody; nothing is booked.

s3.title: Saeed · low sugar at night
s3.context: His glucose sensor drops to 2.7 mmol/L at 03:10 while asleep. He takes gliclazide.
s3.expect: Auto-prompt (L1): fast sugar and a 15-minute recheck → recovered → medicine review within 24 hours heads the pathway; routine checks follow.

k1.title: Khalid · feels fine, never screened
k1.context: 38, smokes, BP rising, cholesterol never measured. Family record: mother’s stroke at 78 and father’s heart attack at 62 are considered but not premature. Consented genomic result: inherited high-cholesterol variant (demo).
k1.expect: No speech check (nothing triggered it). Voice tests: diabetes risk 3, STOP-BANG 4, mood negative. Cholesterol first in the IFHAS blood draw within a month; quit support; the variant and a sleep-study decision go to the doctor.

k3.title: Khalid · chest tightness, then “not now”
k3.context: He reports chest tightness on exertion, then answers “not now” to booking.
k3.expect: Symptoms are not screening (H2): a doctor’s appointment within 1 week heads the pathway. “Not now” pauses the routine checks, but Noa escalates the urgent item to his doctor (U1).

k4.title: Khalid · BP 184/112 today
k4.expect: Noa flags it by itself (B1): urgency today, first in the pathway. No speech check: blood pressure alone does not call for one.

a1.title: Amna · family history beats age
a1.context: 35, diabetes in pregnancy 2021, HbA1c 5.9%; mother had breast cancer at 48 (family record).
a1.expect: HbA1c and cervical screening (overdue, within a month) after 15:30. Under 40 she is outside the breast programme, so a breast risk assessment goes to the doctor.

m1.title: Moza · 78, home after her stroke
m1.context: The signed-in user. 11 days after a stroke with atrial fibrillation; lives alone; hard of hearing; low mood since the stroke. Programme screening has ended at her age.
m1.expect: Noa Speech Check against her own voice (after her stroke). No mammogram, bowel or cervical screening (aged out, by the guideline). Instead: bone density scan (women 65+) and flu vaccine; hearing 1 of 3 → hearing referral; falls and mood follow-up; stroke clinic and BP review for the doctor.

h1.title: Hind · 18-month visit overdue, few words
h1.context: 18 months; mum says 1–2 words. Mother had diabetes in pregnancy (family record).
h1.expect: Vaccines and the 18-month visit within 2 weeks, with M-CHAT-R; growth watched; development review and hearing test for the paediatrician within a month.

d1.title: Hamdan · school entry, squints
d1.context: 5, starts Year 1 in January; squints at screens.
d1.expect: 5-year visit with school-entry vision and hearing; possible eye referral for the paediatrician within a month.

child.ok: Up to date: celebrated, not nudged

why.child: Children are followed by well-child visits, not a heart score
why.cvd: After a heart attack or stroke the clinic manages heart risk directly, so no score
why.under30: The Framingham score is valid from 30, so Noa talks about lifelong habits instead
why.over74: The Framingham score is valid up to 74, so the doctor decides
